::: {#rem-codes-pcp}
#### Codes in the PCP theorem

The PCP [theorem](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/proof-writing.html#def-theorem) says that every statement in NP
has a proof that a randomized verifier can check
by reading a constant number of its [bits](entropy.qmd#def-bit)
and flipping only $\asymub{\log n}$ coins,
where $n$ counts the symbols in the statement.
If the statement is true, some proof makes the verifier accept with [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) 1;
if it is false, every proof makes the verifier reject with probability at least $1/2$.
@arora2009computational [chapter 11] prove a weaker version,
in which the verifier flips polynomially many coins,
by writing the proof in the [Hadamard code](#def-hadamard-code).
The verifier then tests a few positions, picked by coin flips, of the encoded proof,
in the spirit of @thm-hadamard-local-decoding,
instead of reading all of it.
They prove the full result in chapter 22.

:::
